concept_summary: The fantasy of Daily-seed calm logic puzzles replanted on one shared map where every player acts at once and every move is visible. Resources, storms, and scarcities hit everyone simultaneously, so private optimization loses to public negotiation. The game only functions above fifty concurrent players.
first_experiment: Moderated crowd test: put fifteen volunteers on one shared board for twenty minutes; if alliances form without prompting, the social layer carries the game.
why_it_is_opposite: While the source is a private experience, this concept flips it into a crowd: playing alone is impossible here, whereas the source never requires another person.

concept_summary: A reverse-loop game in the world of URL-to-level destruction sandbox: you begin holding everything the source hands out and win by giving it all back. Where the source loop is 'URL-to-level: any pasted website URL becomes the destructible level with 7 weapons plus jetpack', here every move undoes the 'URL-to-level: any pasted website URL becomes the destructible level with 7 weapons plus jetpack' loop step by step instead of advancing it, so the map empties and the score falls. Hoarding triggers the lose state; the end screen celebrates an empty board.
first_experiment: Paper prototype: ten tokens stand in for everything the player owns and each turn must discard at least one; test with five players whether emptying the board feels like winning after three rounds.
why_it_is_opposite: While the source rewards accumulation (URL-to-level: any pasted website URL becomes the destructible level with 7 weapons plus jetpack), this concept rewards the opposite: progress means having less, so a winning run here would score zero in the source.

concept_summary: The same core loop as Local-culture-as-mechanic driving game, rebuilt end to end for newcomers instead of its current crowd. Controls, difficulty, session shape, and rewards assume newcomers: a guided, jargon-free on-ramp for total beginners. Nothing in this build serves the old crowd; one client cannot satisfy both.
first_experiment: Take one level from the source fantasy, apply the inverted tuning only, and playtest with five target players for ten minutes; a quit-rate on the opposite side of half from the source baseline confirms the audience split is real.
why_it_is_opposite: While the source is tuned for its current crowd (players who recognize the source culture, plus curious outsiders: systems tuned for veterans of the genre), this concept flips every tuning decision toward newcomers (a guided, jargon-free on-ramp for total beginners), so the two builds want mutually exclusive players.
